record.what_it_does: Private-market data on companies, deals, investors, funds and LPs, via a contract-gated API.
record.auth_notes: PitchBook's own Postman-hosted API v2 docs confirm a static API key. It is sent on every request as the header "Authorization: PB-Token {API_KEY}". The REST API has no OAuth. Keys belong to the customer organization, and each call spends that organization's API credits (402 means insufficient credit). Production and sandbox use separate keys. Composio's existing PitchBook toolkit uses API_KEY auth. The Premium MCP connector is separate: users sign in with PitchBook SSO through Claude, not with an API key.
record.access_notes: The API is a quote-only add-on. It requires a PitchBook platform subscription plus a separate Direct Data/API contract. Keys and credits come through the account manager, not a self-serve dashboard, and there is no free tier. Every call has a credit cost, and credits are added through the account manager. Sandbox keys are provisioned separately.
record.api_breadth_notes: The base URL is https://api.pitchbook.com, shared by production and sandbox. The API covers Companies, Deals, People, Investors, Funds, Service Providers and Limited Partners, plus credit news and research, patents, fund performance and cash flows, valuation estimates, VC exit predictions, bulk endpoints, and account and credit usage. Composio's PitchBook toolkit wraps 130 tools, so the API is well over 50 operations. A public Postman documenter page exists (documenter.gw.postman.com/view/metadata/TzCV1iRc), but third parties say the full endpoint reference requires a login.
record.mcp_notes: The official server is https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp ("PitchBook Premium"). Claude's marketplace lists it as made by PitchBook. PitchBook help pages describe it as the Premium Connector for Claude, and there is also a ChatGPT version. To use it you need a seat-based, unlimited or trial PitchBook license plus SSO credentials, and a Claude org owner must enable it first. PitchBook currently includes it free for subscribers. Third-party wrappers exist from Strac, Apify, Merge and Vinkius.
record.blocker_notes: The API is public, documented and key-based, and Composio already ships a 130-tool PitchBook toolkit with API_KEY auth, so it can be built. The catch is that each end-user organization must hold a PitchBook subscription plus a separately contracted API add-on with credits. Composio cannot get test credentials without a contract or partnership. The official remote MCP is an alternative for PitchBook license holders.

evidence.quote: include a header named "Authorization" with the value of "PB-Token {API_KEY}" with each API request.
Companies, Deals, People, Investors, Fund, Service Provider and Limited Partner information.
Each request for data to the API will have an associated credit cost.
PitchBook API keys are provisioned as part of a paid API add-on rather than generated self-serve.
PitchBook's API and data feed are quote-only add-ons.
PitchBook also offers a test sandbox environment that uses the same base URL with a separate key.

record.needs_human: pitchbook.com help pages still return 403 to automated fetches, so a human should confirm the MCP licensing and SSO terms there (they come from search snippets of pitchbook.com/help/getting-started-with-pitchbook-premium-connector). It is still unknown whether PitchBook publishes an OpenAPI spec or webhooks.
